Answer: B
Reason: The initial chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates extensive, widespread confluent consolidation confined to the left lung. Subsequent imaging (Figures 3a and 3b) reveals progression to complete opacification of the left hemithorax (consistent with a "white-out" or massive effusion/consolidation) and the development of new patchy airspace opacity in the right upper zone, indicating disease progression and contralateral spread typical of invasive aspergillosis in an immunocompromised host.
